issues.body:
assemble_registry() checks only that the fragment contains at least one regex-matched id. A fragment such as `[[benchmark]]
id="ok"
[[benchmark]]
name="missing"` is accepted, even though the new contract says every entry requires an id. This creates an assembled TOML registry containing an unidentifiable benchmark and can make downstream ID-based gates silently ignore that record. The existing no-id test uses a fragment with only one entry, so it does not exercise this case.
issues.fix_hint: Parse each fragment with tomllib (or otherwise split and validate every [[benchmark]] block), require exactly one non-empty string id per benchmark table, and add a regression test with two entries where only one has an id. Keep duplicate detection over the resulting per-entry IDs. Also make --check reject parse failures directly if parsing is introduced there.
issues.title: ID validation is fragment-wide instead of per benchmark entry

verdict.summary: The fragment architecture and consumer wiring are coherent, but the benchmark assembler does not enforce its stated per-entry ID invariant. A fragment containing multiple [[benchmark]] tables passes as long as any one table has an id, leaving anonymous benchmark records in the assembled registry. The focused tests cover only the single-entry/no-id case and therefore do not catch this.
